Session isolation: one microVM per user session prevents data leaking between sessions; when a session ends, the microVM is terminated and its memory sanitized.

Long sessions: sessions on microVMs run for up to 8 hours, for complex reasoning and asynchronous work; Runtime also offers instance-based compute in your account for multi-day sessions and GPUGPU (Graphics processing unit)A processor with thousands of small cores that run many calculations in parallel. GPUs speed up machine learning, graphics, and video work; EC2 instance families such as P and G include them.Glossary entryClose workloads.
Large inputs: payloads up to 100 MB, so agents can handle images, audio, video, and large datasets.

Protocols: HTTPHTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)The protocol that web browsers and APIs use to send requests, such as GET and POST, and receive responses. On its own it is not encrypted; HTTPS adds TLS.Glossary entryClose and WebSocket streaming, MCP for tools, and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) for agents that talk to other agents.
Versions and endpoints: each deployment creates an immutable version, and named endpoints point to versions, so you can promote a tested version and roll back by moving the endpoint (task 3.3.8).

The agent code (for example a Strands or LangGraph agent) is packaged as a container and deployed to Runtime, often from a CI/CDCI/CD (Continuous integration and continuous delivery)Practices in which every code change is built and tested automatically (continuous integration) and kept ready to release, often deploying it automatically through a pipeline (continuous delivery or deployment).Glossary entryClose pipeline that creates a new version and moves the endpoint after tests pass.
Users sign in through the company identity provider; Identity checks the token and lets the agent call SaaS APIs as that user.
Gateway exposes internal APIs and Lambda functions as MCP tools, and Policy limits which tools and actions each agent may use.
Memory keeps the conversation and long-term facts about each user.
Observability sends traces and metrics to CloudWatch, and Evaluations score quality on sample sessions.
Session isolation in separate microVMs; inbound authentication through your identity provider or IAM; outbound credentials managed by Identity instead of being stored in agent code.

Least privilegeLeast privilegeGiving each person or system only the permissions it needs for its task, and no more. In IAM, this means starting with no access and allowing specific actions on specific resources.Glossary entryClose: the runtime's execution role and Gateway targets get only the permissions their tools need; Policy adds deterministic limits on tool calls.
Guardrails from Amazon Bedrock can filter model inputs and outputs inside the agent; CloudTrail records the AgentCore API calls.

AgentCore runs agents from any framework and model in production, with no infrastructure to manage.
Runtime isolates each session in its own microVM, supports sessions up to 8 hours and 100 MB payloads, and versions agents behind endpoints.
Memory keeps short-term and long-term state; Gateway turns APIs and Lambda functions into MCP tools; Identity and Policy control what agents can reach and do.
Observability traces every step in CloudWatch, and Evaluations measure quality.
Amazon Bedrock Agents (now Agents Classic) is closed to new customers since July 30, 2026; build new agents on AgentCore, with the managed agent harness for a low-code start.

paragraphs: AWS's platform for running AI agents in production with any framework and model: Runtime with isolated sessions, Memory, Gateway for turning APIs into MCP tools, Identity, Policy, Code Interpreter and Browser tools, Observability, Evaluations, versioning, security, cost, and how it differs from Amazon Bedrock Agents.
6 min read · Last reviewed 3 November 2026 · MLA-C02

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform for deploying and operating AI agents securely at scale, with any agent framework (such as Strands Agents, LangGraph, CrewAI, or LlamaIndex) and any foundation model, in or outside Amazon Bedrock. It provides the pieces that an agent needs in production, without infrastructure to manage: a serverless runtime with isolated sessions, memory, a gateway to tools, identity, policy controls, built-in tools, observability, and evaluations. The services work together or on their own.

Choose AgentCore when a question is about running agents in production: isolating each user's session, keeping state across turns and sessions, exposing company APIsAPI (Application programming interface)A defined way for one program to ask another for data or actions, such as a set of HTTPS requests and responses. Every AWS service is controlled through its API, which the console, the CLI, and the SDKs call for you.Glossary entryClose to agents as tools, controlling what agents may do, or tracing and evaluating agent behaviour (MLA-C02 tasks 3.1.6, 3.2.9, 3.2.11, 3.3.8, 4.1.5, and 4.2.8).
A typical production design (task 3.2.11):

Runtime is serverless and scales sessions on demand; persistent filesystems and Memory let agents resume work. Design tools to be idempotentIdempotencyAn operation is idempotent when repeating it has the same effect as doing it once, such as setting a value rather than adding to it. It makes retries safe; many AWS APIs accept a client token for this.Glossary entryClose and add retries for failed tool calls.

Fast cold startsCold startThe extra delay when AWS Lambda must create a new execution environment, load the code, and run its initialization before handling a request. Later requests reuse the environment and are faster; provisioned concurrency avoids cold starts.Glossary entryClose for real-time chats, streaming responses, and long sessions for slower reasoning. Watch for tool failures, coordination failures between agents, and truncated streaming in Observability traces (task 4.1.5).

Pricing is consumption-based with no upfront commitment. Runtime charges for resources actually used, and CPU is typically not billed while the agent waits on a model or I/O. Model tokens are billed separately by the model provider (for example Amazon Bedrock), so monitor token usage per agent and cache or shorten prompts (tasks 4.2.8 and 4.2.10).

AgentCore Observability shows sessions, traces, and spans in CloudWatch, with metrics such as latencyLatencyThe time between sending a request and receiving the response, usually measured in milliseconds. Distance and processing add to it; caching and serving users from nearby locations reduce it.Glossary entryClose, errors, and token use; the OpenTelemetry format also works with other observability tools. Use AWS X-Ray and CloudWatch for the AWS services that the agent's tools call (task 4.2.2).

rows: Service
What it does
Answers the requirement
Runtime
Hosts agents and tools serverlessly; each user session runs in its own microVM with isolated CPU, memory, and filesystem, wiped when the session ends
Isolation between users, long-running or asynchronous agents, any framework
Memory
Short-term memory of turns within a session, and long-term memory that extracts preferences, facts, and summaries across sessions
Agents that remember context and users (agent state management)
Gateway
Turns APIs, Lambda functions, and existing services into Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and connects to existing MCP servers
Give agents access to company tools without rewriting them
Identity

Authenticates users into agents through existing identity providers (such as Amazon Cognito, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID), and lets agents call third-party services with OAuth or API keys on a user's behalf
Agents act with the right user's permissions
Policy
Deterministic rules, written in natural language or a Cedar-compatible policy language, checked on every tool call through Gateway
Agents stay within business rules and allowed actions
Code Interpreter
An isolated sandbox where agents run code (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript)
Calculations and data analysis inside the agent
Browser
A managed cloud browser that agents use to navigate websites and fill forms
Tasks in web applications without an API
Observability
Traces each step: reasoning, tool calls, and model interactions, in OpenTelemetry format, shown in Amazon CloudWatch
Debug failures and bottlenecks, audit agent decisions
Evaluations
Automated assessment of how well agents and tools complete tasks, before and after deployment
Measure agent quality over time

Choose
An agent declared by configuration (model, tools, instructions), little code
AgentCore's managed agent harness
An existing agent built with Bedrock action groups

Your own agent code in any framework or model, run in production with isolation, memory, and tracing
